Application FAQs
Application FAQs
If you don't see an answer to your question, please contact
graduateadmissions@mail.wvu.edu.
Application Fees
How do I qualify for an application fee waiver?
Applicants are eligible for an application fee waiver from the Office of
Graduate Admissions and Recruitment if one of the following criteria applies:
Current WVU or WVU Medicine (full-time, and/or benefits eligible) employee
Current, active United States Military personnel or Veteran
PeaceCorps or Americorps Member
I am an International Applicant and am experiencing difficulty submitting the
application fee.
If you are receiving an error during payment submission, please contact
internationaladmissions@mail.wvu.edu.
Application Status Meaning
I have submitted my application, can you please let me know its status?
*Note: Your application may skip some statuses and not all statuses will apply
to your intended graduate program application process.
Application Submitted
-
This means your application has been submitted but has not yet been
processed.
Pending
- This means your application has been submitted, processed, and WVU
is waiting to receive your
official undergraduate transcripts.
Complete
- This means your
application is complete, that it includes all WVU and
intended graduate program specific documents
.
Out to Department
- This means your application AND official transcripts have been received
and sent electronically to the intended graduate program department for review.
Your application will be sent to the department regardless of any department
required documents. If your application does not move to the next status in
a timely manner, please contact your intended graduate program department to
determine why the application review process has paused.
Waitlist
- This means your application has been reviewed and placed on a waitlist.
You should contact your intended graduate program department for further information.
Interview
- This means your application has been reviewed and you have been chosen
for an interview with your intended graduate program department. You should
contact your intended graduate program department for further information.
Transcripts
Can I submit unofficial transcripts?
Domestic (U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident), and International non-health
science students can use unofficial transcripts for an admission decision
– they will have to send their official transcripts (to show they have earned
the bachelor’s degree and have the minimum GPA) if they are accepted into
a program.
Domestic health science students must submit their official transcripts for
an admission decision.
Program Application Deadlines/Requirements
Where can I find my program of interest's application deadline and/or application
requirements?
Please review the application (deadline / requirements) online via the
graduate admissions database.
I want to talk with a representative from my program. How can I find their
information?
Please review the program contacts for each program online via the
graduate admissions database.
Recommendations
I am having trouble submitting my recommendation for a student. How can
I troubleshoot?
View our
recommenders page and make sure you are following all of the steps
correctly for the best experience. If you are still having difficulties
afterward, please contact our office via email at
graduateadmissions@mail.wvu.edu.
